title: A Slot in the Student Gallery

script.speaker: student
script.text: Hi. Are you the person who looks after the student gallery? I'm hoping to book a slot for the spring.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: That's me. Have a seat. What have you got?

script.speaker: student
script.text: It's a photography series. I've been shooting the old rail yard behind campus for about a year. I heard a slot had opened up in the main room.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: It did, but somebody took it on Monday. The main room's full right through to the end of term. I'm sorry.

script.speaker: student
script.text: Oh. So there's nothing left at all?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: I didn't say that. The corridor space is free. That's the long wall by the west stairs.

script.speaker: student
script.text: The corridor. Right. Isn't that where they put the flyers about parking?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Not any more. We cleared it out last year and put in a proper hanging rail.

script.speaker: student
script.text: A rail?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: You can't get a nail into those walls. They're concrete behind the paint. So there's a rail along the top, and the work hangs off it on cables.

script.speaker: student
script.text: That's a problem. My whole plan was one long panorama. Three panels side by side, about twelve feet across.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Then no. The cables hang straight down, so everything sits in columns. You'd want smaller prints, stacked, maybe two or three on a cable.

script.speaker: student
script.text: But the scale is the point. You're meant to stand in front of it and feel small.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: I know, and I'm not telling you to drop it. I'm telling you what the wall can do. Can I say one thing for the corridor?

script.speaker: student
script.text: Go ahead.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Everyone walks past it. Every person heading to the lecture halls comes down those stairs. The main room's lovely, but the door's locked unless somebody's sitting in there, and most days nobody is.

script.speaker: student
script.text: So people just walk by it.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: They do. I've watched them. And the corridor has glass along the south side, so it's lit all day. You don't have to switch anything on.

script.speaker: student
script.text: Okay. That's not nothing. How many cables are there?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Eight. They slide along the rail, so you're not stuck with even spacing.

script.speaker: student
script.text: Eight columns. I could break the panorama into a grid. It wouldn't be the same piece, but it might still work.

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: It'd be a different piece. That isn't always a bad thing.

script.speaker: student
script.text: Can I go and look at it first, before I decide anything?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Please do. It's open now. If you want the slot, fill in the request form and get it back to me by the end of next week. And bring a sketch of the layout with it. I can't approve a wall I can't picture.

script.speaker: student
script.text: Right. Which way is it from here?

script.speaker: coordinator
script.text: Out of the office and left. You can't miss it.

questions.question: What are the speakers mainly discussing?

choices.A: How the wall in the corridor by the west stairs should be repaired
choices.B: Where and in what form the student can show her photographs
choices.C: Which photographs the student ought to include in her series
choices.D: Why the main gallery room stays locked for most of the day

questions.explanation: 学生は冒頭で「I'm hoping to book a slot for the spring.」と用件を告げ、担当者が「The corridor space is free.」と代わりの場所を出す。以降は「the work hangs off it on cables」という掛け方と、「I could break the panorama into a grid.」という並べ方の相談で会話が進む。展示の場所と形が終始の話題なので B。A の修繕は話題にならない。担当者が言うのは「We cleared it out last year and put in a proper hanging rail.」という設置済みの設備の説明であって、壁を直す話ではない。C は写真の選び方だが、どの写真を入れるかは一度も出ず、話題は大きさと配置に限られる。D の施錠は「the door's locked unless somebody's sitting in there」と一度だけ、廊下の利点を裏づける材料として触れられるだけで主題ではない。

questions.question: According to the coordinator, why can the student not hang her work on the corridor wall as she had planned?

choices.A: The corridor wall is too short for the panorama she has in mind
choices.B: The gallery lends out frames in one standard size only
choices.C: Another student has already reserved the corridor for the spring
choices.D: Nails will not go into the wall, so the work must hang from cables

questions.explanation: 担当者は「You can't get a nail into those walls. They're concrete behind the paint. So there's a rail along the top, and the work hangs off it on cables.」と理由を述べ、続けて「The cables hang straight down, so everything sits in columns.」と、縦に並ぶという制約を説明する。だから D。A の壁の長さは問題にされていない。担当者はその壁を「the long wall by the west stairs」と呼んでおり、短さは一度も理由に挙がらない。B の額縁は会話に一切出てこない。C は事実と逆で、押さえられたのは本館の枠(「somebody took it on Monday」)であり、廊下については「The corridor space is free.」と明言されている。

questions.question: Why does the coordinator point out that the door of the main room is usually locked?

choices.A: To argue that more people would actually see the work in the corridor
choices.B: To explain how the main room came to be booked so quickly
choices.C: To warn the student that she would have to carry her own key
choices.D: To apologise for a rule that he himself does not agree with

questions.explanation: 担当者は「Can I say one thing for the corridor?」と断ってから「Everyone walks past it. Every person heading to the lecture halls comes down those stairs. The main room's lovely, but the door's locked unless somebody's sitting in there, and most days nobody is.」と続ける。廊下を推す文脈で本館の施錠を出しているので、目的は人目に触れる量の比較、つまり A。B は原因が別で、本館が埋まったのは「somebody took it on Monday」という先着の話であり、鍵とは無関係。C の鍵は学生が持つ持たないという話が一度も出ない。D は謝罪でも規則への不満でもない。担当者は施錠を欠点として利用しているだけで、規則への評価は述べていない。

questions.question: How does the student's attitude toward the corridor change during the conversation?

choices.A: She is pleased at first and then becomes worried about the cost
choices.B: She is confident at first and then doubts she can finish in time
choices.C: She treats it as second best at first and then begins to see its value
choices.D: She is unconvinced at the start and remains unconvinced at the end

questions.explanation: 最初は「Oh. So there's nothing left at all?」と落胆し、「The corridor. Right. Isn't that where they put the flyers about parking?」と格下扱いする。しかし人通りと採光の説明を聞いて「Okay. That's not nothing.」と態度を変え、「Eight columns. I could break the panorama into a grid.」と自分から使い方を考え始める。よって C。A は費用の話が皆無で、しかも最初は喜んでいない。B の制作が間に合うかどうかも一度も話題にならない。D は後半と矛盾する。最後も「Can I go and look at it first, before I decide anything?」と自分から現地を見に行こうとしており、疑いのままではない。

questions.question: What does the coordinator ask the student to hand in together with the request form?

choices.A: A list giving the title of each photograph in the series
choices.B: A sketch showing how the work would be laid out on the wall
choices.C: A letter of support from the teacher of her photography course
choices.D: A note stating the total weight of the panels she wants to hang

questions.explanation: 担当者は最後に「fill in the request form and get it back to me by the end of next week. And bring a sketch of the layout with it. I can't approve a wall I can't picture.」と述べる。求めているのは配置の図なので B。A の題名の一覧は会話に出ない。C の指導教員も推薦状も一度も言及されない。D の重量については、担当者が述べる制約は「The cables hang straight down, so everything sits in columns.」という並び方であって重さではなく、重さの数値を求める場面はない。

questions.question: What will the student most probably do immediately after this conversation?

choices.A: Ask a different office for permission to put nails in the wall
choices.B: Abandon the panorama and start photographing a new subject
choices.C: Fill in the request form and hand it back before she leaves
choices.D: Walk over to the corridor and look at the space for herself

questions.explanation: 学生は「Can I go and look at it first, before I decide anything?」と現地を先に見たいと申し出、担当者は「Please do. It's open now.」と応じる。最後に学生は「Right. Which way is it from here?」と道順を尋ね、担当者が「Out of the office and left. You can't miss it.」と答えて会話が終わる。行き先は廊下しかないので、次の行動は現地を見に行くこと、つまり D。A は釘の使用を別の窓口に掛け合う話だが、学生は「You can't get a nail into those walls.」という条件を受け入れており、掛け合う素振りはない。B は逆で、彼女は題材を捨てるどころか「I could break the panorama into a grid. It wouldn't be the same piece, but it might still work.」と同じ作品の作り替えを考えている。C は本人が「before I decide anything」と決定を保留し、しかも道順を聞いて出て行くため、その場で用紙を出すとは読めない。締切も「by the end of next week」と先にある。
